title: Kafka layers: clients, brokers, storage, replicas, controllers
outcome: Follow one record through discovery, batching, append storage, replication, and consumer fetch.
useCase: Debugging Kafka by layer instead of treating it as one box.
benefits: A concrete model for network, storage, and coordination symptoms.
drawbacks: A local flow demo cannot certify production durability or performance.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes
cue: Client → leader log → replicas; controller manages metadata.

trace.title: Client library
trace.detail: The client library handles protocol requests, metadata, batching, retries, and serialization integration. A bootstrap address helps discover the cluster. The client then communicates with relevant broker endpoints; bootstrap is not a permanent universal proxy.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
The producer discovers leader endpoints, sends a batch, and receives an acknowledgement under its configuration. A consumer fetches retained records from assigned partitions. It does not require the producer process to remain alive after durable publication.

When a client cannot connect after initial discovery, inspect advertised listeners/DNS/network/auth for actual broker addresses. When append latency rises, inspect broker/storage/replica health rather than only Rails CPU.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: One local broker hides replica/failover behavior. Acknowledgement settings cannot create replicas that do not exist. Confusing controller roles with business consumers makes diagnosis random.
